Quotes state the change goes only from disabled to enabled and cannot be reverted, and that you can revert from cluster mode compatible to disabled preserving the original configurations.
Quotes state Multi-AZ is on by default for cluster mode enabled clusters and is automatically enabled only with at least one replica in a different AZ from the primary in all shards.
Quoted conditions list: keys in database 0 only, a cluster-protocol client using a configuration endpoint, and auto-failover with at least 1 replica; the claim says 'including'.

Quotes state the two-step procedure that keeps availability, compatible mode allowing either protocol, enabled as the second step after compatible, and no scaling or engine version changes in compatible mode.

Cost to scale quote states it word for word: costly scaling for extremely high reads, needing several read replicas to match one in-memory cache node in requests per second.
Quotes state ElastiCache for Valkey supports durability for caching and data store workloads with microsecond read latency, currently supported with node-based ElastiCache.
Under 'Choose Memcached if the following apply for you', the four quoted items match: simplest model, large multi-core nodes, scaling out and in by nodes, caching objects.

Under the Multi-AZ 'entire cluster fails' heading, quotes give nodes recreated in the same AZs, all data lost, and that this is rare; the Replication note gives recovery from the transactional log with durability.
Quote states evictions usually mean scale up or out, with the exception for purposely relying on eviction (LRU cache) carried in the quote.
Quote states evictions occur when memory is overfilled or above maxmemory and keys are chosen by the selected eviction policy.
FAQ quote states one free snapshot per active cache and additional storage from $0.085/GiB every month for all Regions.
FAQ quote states upgrading via Modify and the Cache Engine Version field, applied immediately if checked or in the next maintenance window.
FAQ quote: up to 300 reserved nodes in the same Region; request a quota increase for more.

FAQ quote states in-place upgrade without downtime from any supported Redis OSS version to any Valkey version, with the 30 to 60 second DNS failover exception below 5.0.6.
Quote states replication from primary to a secondary created in another chosen Region, and that ElastiCache sets up and manages automatic, asynchronous replication.
Quote states double-digit millisecond response times at best despite optimization, assuming steady load and optimal performance.
Under lazy loading disadvantages, quotes state the miss penalty with three trips per miss and the noticeable delay.
Under lazy loading advantages, quote states a replaced empty node leaves the app functioning with increased latency, misses query the database and data is added to the cache.
Quotes state the configuration endpoint for instance-based Memcached with Automatic Discovery, and individual node endpoints tracked as nodes change without it.

Quotes state failover to a read replica with possible loss from async replication, and with durability no acknowledged loss (sync) or up to 10 seconds (async).
Quote states node-based clusters for fine-grained control, choosing node type, number of nodes and AZ placement.
Quoted list ('most effective for the following workload types') gives read-heavy repeated queries on rarely changing data, expensive queries, and high concurrency reducing database CPU pressure.
Quota table row with header: Nodes per Region, default 300 each supported Region, adjustable Yes, across all clusters, 300 reserved plus 300 non-reserved.
RBAC page quote: RBAC is the only way to control access to serverless caches, available for Valkey 7.2 onward and Redis OSS 6.0 to 7.2.
Quote: reserved-memory-percent defaults to 25%, do not reduce it, a lower reserve can cause data loss especially during upgrades or changes.
Quote states memory can double or more in forked bgsave or full sync, and the automatic forkless switch on insufficient FreeableMemory, which uses less memory but can add latency.

Quote: Serverless supports 30K ECPUs/second on an empty cache and up to 90K ECPUs/sec with Read from Replica.
Quotes state node-based uses 6379, serverless uses 6379 and 6380, and 6380 must be accessible even without Read From Replica because many clients connect to both ports.
Under the 'Pre-scaling with ElastiCache Serverless' heading, quote states minimum limits for ECPUs per second or storage, also called pre-warming, useful before anticipated scaling events.
Quotes state two endpoints for different consistency needs with the same DNS name and different ports, and automatic routing of reads to a local-AZ replica when possible.
Whitepaper quotes state scaling up with a larger node type or down with a smaller one, and scaling out reads with replicas and writes with new shards.
Quote advises scaling when traffic is at a minimum; scaling is designed to stay online, but this helps data sync to newer nodes.
Under Adding TTL, quote states an expired key is treated as not found, the database is queried and the cache updated, with no staleness guarantee but periodic refresh.
Quote: even if not stale, cached data should always be treated as stale, and candidacy depends on the application's tolerance for stale data.

PERF03-BP05 'Common anti-patterns' list quoted with the two items: caching frequently changing data and relying on cache as durable and always available.
Quotes define client-side caching and state that multiple clients may store the same data, causing duplicate storage and inconsistency.
Quotes state remote cache gives consistent responses and more cached data because storage scales independently of clients, with higher latency from the extra network hop.

Quotes state the non-Multi-AZ path (new primary, sync from replica or empty with data loss unless restored, longer write interruption) and the auto-failover-without-Multi-AZ note with no AZ-level protection.
Quotes define write-through and, under its disadvantages heading, state most data is never read, which is a waste of resources.

The quote 'Which adds latency to the process' has its subject (every write involves two trips, cache and database) only in the surrounding text, so the cause and the write-process scope are not in the quote; the tolerance sentence is supported.
